Nevertheless, the sustained WVTR after accelerated aging indicates the suitability of the Aluzine and Masterbond epoxies to act as a reliable component within the inorganic/polymer-composite multilayer system. In the next section, we evaluate the optoelectronic properties of TCO/ultra-thin metal/TCO (TMT) structures and their capabilities to reduce permeability. Overall, the RF magnetron sputtering was identified as the limiting factor in reducing WVTRs, and significant improvements would require an ALD system. Since the procurement of an ALD system was not viable by the time of this revelation, substantial reductions in WVTRs were not obtained. Nevertheless, procurement is underway to facilitate continued progress. Optoelectronic Properties of TCO/Metal/TCO Inorganic Multilayers – Prior work from NREL suggested that a sputtered TCO/nanolayer-metal/TCO multilayer structure is capable of decreasing WVTR up to 1,000 times (measured at 25˚C and 40% R.H.) while maintaining optical transmission comparable to, and electrical conductivities better than a single TCO layer.48 Material candidates most pertinent to our multi-layer barrier structures were identified from previous studies as Ag and IZO, 48 as the Ag offers very low resistivity (1.6 µΩ·cm) with low absorptivity in the visible region for very thin layers (approximately 10nm),140 while the IZO exhibits good optoelectronic properties and stability under damp heat exposure (>1,000 hrs. at 85˚C 85% R.H.).141 With this TMT structure identified, HNEI ramped up the capabilities of room temperature RF magnetron sputtering for the integration of an IZO/Ag-nanolayer film on a single substrate. As a result, 200nm thick IZO layers with resistivity near the typical value of 6.6E-04 Ω·cm were demonstrated, with an average transparency of 85.7% between the 350nm – 850nm wavelength range, pertinent to perovskite photovoltaics. The transparency of IZO was observed to increase to above 90% transmission with the incorporation of oxygen partial pressure and reduction in thickness, however, at the detriment of electrical conductivity. Furthermore, ultra-thin Ag film of thickness 10 ± 3 nm sputtered on soda-lime glass (SLG) demonstrated resistivity of 3.32E-06 Ω·cm, near the bulk resistivity of Ag (1.6E-06 Ω·cm), and an averaged optical transparency of 52.3% in the 400nm-850nm range (normalized to the optical transparency of SLG).
